rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even when pregnancy reported unlikely; pelvic ultrasound assesses uterus and ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; high FSH + low estrogen → ovarian failure
Low/normal FSH + low estrogen → hypothalamic/pituitary cause; persistent unexplained prolactin elevation → pituitary MRI
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough, daytime somnolence suggest ventilatory muscle weakness
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread active/chronic denervation; sensory conduction usually normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transvaginal imaging safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, severe agitation; **clozapine** for resistant schizophrenia or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: increased mortality; reserve for dangerous/severely distressing behavior after safer measures

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

asplenia.name: Asplenia
asplenia.scope: Anatomic asplenia (splenectomy), functional asplenia (sickle cell), Howell-Jolly bodies, reactive thrombocytosis, encapsulated organism sepsis (Streptococcus pneumoniae), vaccination timing, antibiotic prophylaxis
asplenia.core: Absent or poorly functioning spleen impairs clearance of encapsulated organisms; fever can progress rapidly to fatal sepsis despite prior vaccination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Splenectomy for trauma/hematologic disease; functional loss with sickle cell disease; congenital absence
Sepsis risk greatest early after surgery and in children, but remains lifelong

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fever, rigors, malaise, vomiting, or rapid deterioration → **overwhelming postsplenectomy infection**
Pneumococcus especially important; also meningococcus, Hib; dog bites risk Capnocytophaga
Travel-associated malaria and Babesia can become unusually severe

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of splenic macrophage filtration and IgM memory B-cell function impairs opsonized-organism clearance
Reduced removal of erythrocyte inclusions and platelets explains characteristic blood findings

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Smear: **Howell–Jolly bodies**; reactive thrombocytosis after splenectomy; correlate with history/imaging
Febrile illness → cultures, CBC, lactate, source evaluation; do not delay antibiotics for results
Unexplained anemia/fever after tick exposure or travel → smear/PCR for intraerythrocytic parasites

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected sepsis → **immediate ceftriaxone**, add vancomycin for severe/resistant pneumococcal concern
Resuscitate and admit if ill; even initially mild fever requires urgent clinical evaluation
Standby oral antibiotic if immediate care inaccessible, followed by emergency evaluation; not a substitute for assessment
Daily penicillin/amoxicillin in young children, particularly sickle cell disease through at least age 5

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant bacteremia, meningitis, purpura fulminans, DIC, death
Postoperative thrombosis risk; isolated reactive platelet elevation does not automatically require antiplatelet treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vaccinate **≥14 days before elective splenectomy**; after emergency surgery vaccinate once stable
Adult antibiotic prophylaxis individualized by postoperative period, immune status, and prior invasive infection
Medical alert ID, fever plan, influenza vaccination; bite counseling, travel precautions and malaria prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron deficiency: reactive thrombocytosis without splenic dysfunction
Hyposplenism: spleen present but impaired; similar infection precautions

table.title: Vaccine priorities: unvaccinated adults
rows: One dose if not previously vaccinated

atrial-fibrillation.name: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.scope: Rate and rhythm control, stroke prevention (CHA2DS2-VASc), unstable AF, embolic complications
atrial-fibrillation.core: Disorganized atrial activation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm and left atrial appendage thromboembolism risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, hypertension, heart failure, coronary disease, obesity, sleep apnea
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol binges, infection, postoperative stress, mitral valve disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, exercise intolerance, dyspnea; sometimes incidental or first detected after stroke
★ **Hypotension, ischemic chest pain, pulmonary edema, altered mentation** → unstable AF
Very rapid irregular wide-complex rhythm suggests preexcitation; ordinary AV nodal blockers can be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary-vein ectopic triggers plus atrial remodeling sustain reentry
Loss of atrial contraction reduces filling; persistent tachycardia can impair LV function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG: absent discrete P waves**, variable RR intervals; document rhythm rather than pulse alone
TSH, electrolytes, renal function; transthoracic echocardiogram for ventricular function and structural disease
Intermittent symptoms → ambulatory rhythm monitoring; assess reversible triggers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → **synchronized cardioversion**; do not delay for anticoagulation or TEE
Stable rate control: metoprolol or diltiazem; avoid diltiazem/verapamil with reduced EF
Decompensated HF: digoxin or amiodarone; preexcited AF: procainamide or cardioversion, no AV nodal blockers
Rhythm control for symptoms, early disease, or HF: cardioversion, selected antiarrhythmics, catheter ablation
★ Duration ≥48 hours/unknown: **3 weeks anticoagulation or TEE** before elective cardioversion; ≥4 weeks afterward

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic emboli to brain, mesentery, limbs; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
Anticoagulant bleeding; rhythm drugs may cause proarrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Long-term anticoagulation: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 men/≥3 women**; consider one point lower
Apixaban/other DOAC preferred; mechanical valve or moderate/severe rheumatic mitral stenosis → warfarin
Weight reduction, BP/OSA treatment, limit alcohol; aspirin does not substitute for anticoagulation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atrial flutter: sawtooth atrial activity, often regular 2:1 conduction
Multifocal atrial tachycardia: ≥3 P-wave morphologies, isoelectric intervals

atrioventricular-block.name: Atrioventricular block
atrioventricular-block.scope: First-degree, second-degree Mobitz type I (Wenckebach), second-degree Mobitz type II, third-degree (complete) AV block, atropine, pacemaker indications
atrioventricular-block.core: Impaired atrial-to-ventricular conduction ranges from harmless delay to complete dissociation; symptoms and level of block determine urgency and pacing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age-related conduction fibrosis, MI, beta blockers, verapamil/diltiazem, digoxin, hyperkalemia
Lyme carditis, infiltrative disease, myocarditis, cardiac surgery; high vagal tone causes benign nodal delay

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, exertional intolerance, presyncope/syncope; cannon A waves with AV dissociation
★ Hypotension, confusion, ischemic discomfort, acute heart failure → **symptomatic unstable bradycardia**
Wide QRS and slow escape suggest distal disease; narrow escape may still be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: AV-nodal block often responds to vagal withdrawal; His–Purkinje failure risks unpredictable progression and asystole

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **12-lead ECG** establishes conduction pattern; continuous monitoring for significant block
Review drugs, electrolytes, ischemia; targeted Lyme testing with exposure; echo for structural disease
2:1 block cannot be labeled Mobitz I versus II from ratio alone; assess QRS and localization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → airway/oxygen if needed, IV access, **atropine** while preparing pacing
★ Atropine ineffective or distal high-grade block → **transcutaneous pacing**, then temporary transvenous pacing
Epinephrine/dopamine infusion can bridge to pacing; confirm electrical and mechanical capture
Stop AV-nodal blockers and correct reversible cause; do not wait for atropine in deteriorating infranodal disease
Permanent pacing for acquired Mobitz II, high-grade, or complete block without reversible cause, even asymptomatic

rows.label: Complications
items: Adams–Stokes syncope, low-output failure, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death
Pacemaker implantation → infection, pneumothorax, lead problems; prolonged RV pacing may impair LV function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, ischemia/electrolyte treatment; asymptomatic first-degree or nodal Mobitz I usually observation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blocked premature atrial beat: early hidden P wave, noncompensatory pause
Sinus arrest: absent P waves during pause
AV dissociation from VT: ventricular tachycardia drives rhythm

table.title: ECG distinction
rows: Progressive PR lengthening, then dropped QRS
Constant conducted PR, sudden dropped QRS

autoimmune-blistering-diseases.name: Autoimmune blistering diseases
autoimmune-blistering-diseases.scope: Bullous pemphigoid (hemidesmosomes, BP180/BP230, tense bullae, linear IF), pemphigus vulgaris (desmoglein, flaccid bullae, oral lesions, intraepidermal acantholysis, reticular IF), dermatitis herpetiformis
autoimmune-blistering-diseases.core: Blister morphology, mucosal involvement, biopsy level, and direct immunofluorescence distinguish major autoimmune blistering diseases and guide immunosuppression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bullous pemphigoid: older adults, neurologic disease, selected drugs; pemphigus: middle-aged adults
Dermatitis herpetiformis: celiac disease and gluten exposure; review new medications and systemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fragile mucosal disease can impair **oral intake** before widespread cutaneous involvement
Extensive denudation, fever, dehydration, ocular symptoms → urgent inpatient/specialist evaluation
Nikolsky sign: lateral pressure shears epidermis; supports pemphigus but is not uniquely diagnostic

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Autoantibodies disrupt epidermal cell adhesion or dermal–epidermal anchoring; blister depth determines fragility
Dermatitis herpetiformis reflects gluten-associated IgA deposition; intestinal disease may be minimally symptomatic

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two biopsies**: lesional edge for routine histology, normal-appearing perilesional skin for direct IF
Serum antigen-specific antibodies support diagnosis and monitoring; tissue pattern remains central
Suspected dermatitis herpetiformis → total IgA and IgA anti-tTG; assess iron/nutrient deficiency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pemphigus vulgaris → **rituximab plus systemic glucocorticoid**; protect wounds, fluids, nutrition
★ Bullous pemphigoid → **potent topical corticosteroid**; systemic treatment when extensive or refractory
Doxycycline or steroid-sparing agents selected according to severity, frailty, and response
Dermatitis herpetiformis → **gluten-free diet + dapsone** for rapid skin control; check G6PD before dapsone

rows.label: Complications
items: Skin barrier loss → infection, fluid/protein loss; immunosuppression → opportunistic infection and steroid toxicity
Dapsone → hemolysis, methemoglobinemia; untreated celiac disease → malabsorption and increased lymphoma risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit drugs; infection/vaccine review before immunosuppression; gluten-free dietary adherence

rows.label: Mimics
items: SJS/TEN: acute drug-associated painful necrosis, multisite mucositis
Bullous impetigo: superficial bacterial bullae, honey crust, no autoimmune IF
Porphyria cutanea tarda: sun-exposed hand fragility, elevated porphyrins

table.title: Biopsy distinctions
rows: Pruritic tense bullae; mucosa usually spared
Flaccid bullae, erosions; oral lesions common

autoimmune-blistering-diseases.evidence: Not checked online; established autoimmune blistering-disease teaching.

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.name: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.scope: Asymptomatic cyst, symptomatic cyst, acute Bartholin abscess, incision and drainage, Word catheter placement, marsupialization, excision for recurrent or older women
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.core: Obstructed posterior vestibular gland causing a cyst or abscess; durable drainage prevents recurrence, and age determines the need for malignancy assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive age, prior duct obstruction, previous cyst/abscess; usually polymicrobial vaginal/enteric flora
STIs may coexist but most abscesses are not solely gonococcal or chlamydial

rows.label: Clues
items: Cyst: soft fluctuant, often painless; abscess: marked tenderness, erythema, difficulty sitting/walking
Gland location near 4 or 8 o'clock at vaginal opening; usually unilateral
Firm, fixed, irregular, recurrent, or postmenopausal lesion → malignancy concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Duct occlusion retains gland secretions; bacterial infection produces purulence
Drainage without an epithelialized outlet allows rapid closure and recurrence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical vulvar examination**; assess cellulitis, systemic illness, pregnancy, immune status
GC/chlamydia NAAT when sexual risk or cervicitis; culture selected recurrent/severe infections
★ **Biopsy at age ≥40 or suspicious mass**; imaging unnecessary for typical superficial lesion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Management branches below; **Word catheter about 4 weeks** permits an epithelialized drainage tract
★ Avoid **incision alone or needle aspiration**: rapid closure causes recurrence
Antibiotics only for cellulitis, systemic infection, immunocompromise, or confirmed STI; uncomplicated drainage needs none
Persistent recurrence → gland excision after acute inflammation settles

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, surrounding cellulitis, rare sepsis; early catheter expulsion can compromise tract formation
Excision → bleeding, scarring, dyspareunia; older patients risk missed gland malignancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete catheter follow-up, hygiene without irritating products; condoms/STI treatment for exposure-related infection
No proven universal prevention of duct obstruction; return promptly for recurrent pain, fever, or mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Skene duct cyst: periurethral/anterior location
Epidermal inclusion cyst: superficial skin nodule, possible punctum
Hidradenitis: recurrent multiple intertriginous nodules, sinus tracts

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.evidence: Not checked online; established gynecologic office-procedure teaching.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery, incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Partial obstruction may still permit stool or diarrhea; bowel movements do not exclude early obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; syncope or ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker; alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
carpal-tunnel-syndrome.scope: Median nerve entrapment, pregnancy and endocrine risk factors, Phalen and Tinel tests, wrist splinting, corticosteroid injection, surgical release
carpal-tunnel-syndrome.core: Median nerve compression at the wrist causes nocturnal paresthesias in the thumb, index, middle, and radial ring fingers.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pregnancy/fluid retention, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis
Forceful repetitive hand activity, wrist trauma; dialysis-associated amyloid in selected patients

rows.label: Clues
items: Shaking hand relieves symptoms; driving or sustained wrist flexion aggravates symptoms
★ **Thenar weakness/atrophy**, dropping objects, impaired thumb opposition → advanced nerve injury
Central palm sensation usually spared because palmar cutaneous branch bypasses tunnel
Bilateral symptoms common; isolated little-finger symptoms argue against median neuropathy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Raised pressure beneath transverse carpal ligament → median nerve ischemia/demyelination
Long-standing compression progresses to axonal loss and persistent motor impairment

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical history + **Phalen/Tinel or carpal compression** findings support clinical diagnosis
Phalen: sustained wrist flexion; Tinel: percussion over median nerve reproduces distal paresthesia
★ **Nerve-conduction studies/EMG** for atypical presentation, severity assessment, or uncertain diagnosis before surgery
Targeted TSH/glucose testing when systemic disease suspected; routine wrist imaging unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild/moderate → **neutral-position wrist splint at night**, ergonomic modification
Local corticosteroid injection for persistent symptoms or short-term relief; pregnancy often resolves postpartum
★ Severe deficit, denervation, or failed conservative care → **surgical carpal tunnel release**
NSAIDs do not relieve the underlying compression; avoid repeated ineffective analgesic-only management

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent sensory loss and thenar wasting if severe compression persists
Injection → transient hyperglycemia, rare nerve injury; surgery → scar pain or incomplete release

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reduce prolonged wrist flexion/extension and forceful vibration; adjust workstation and tools
Manage contributing endocrine/inflammatory disease; reassess worsening motor function promptly

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: neck pain, dermatomal weakness/reflex changes
Ulnar neuropathy: little finger/ulnar ring symptoms, interosseous weakness
Pronator syndrome: proximal forearm pain with palmar sensory involvement

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established peripheral nerve localization and management.

cataracts.name: Cataracts
cataracts.scope: Nuclear sclerotic, cortical, posterior subcapsular, painless vision loss, night driving glare, halos around lights, loss of red reflex, phacoemulsification
cataracts.core: Progressive lens clouding causes painless blurred vision, glare, and impaired daily activities; surgery restores optical clarity.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging, diabetes, smoking, ultraviolet exposure, ocular trauma
Chronic glucocorticoids and radiation; congenital cases: genetic disease or intrauterine infection

rows.label: Clues
items: Night driving difficulty, halos around headlights, faded colors, reduced contrast
★ **Diminished red reflex**, lens opacity; monocular diplopia possible
No afferent pupillary defect from uncomplicated lens disease; pain/redness suggests another diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Lens protein aggregation and altered hydration scatter light before it reaches the retina
Diabetes: sorbitol accumulation accelerates osmotic lens damage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Slit-lamp examination** after visual acuity and refraction; dilated fundus examination
Assess retinal disease before surgery; ultrasound when dense opacity blocks fundus visualization
Infant leukocoria → urgent ophthalmology; exclude retinoblastoma rather than assuming cataract

rows.label: Tx
items: Early functional preservation: updated glasses, brighter lighting, glare reduction
★ Function-limiting impairment → **phacoemulsification + intraocular lens**; no visual-acuity threshold required
Congenital visually significant opacity → prompt treatment to prevent deprivation amblyopia

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated severe disease: falls, driving impairment; neglected hypermature lens: inflammation or secondary glaucoma
Surgical: endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, cystoid macular edema
★ Later recurrent haze: **posterior capsule opacification → Nd:YAG capsulotomy**

rows.label: Prevention
items: UV-blocking eyewear, smoking cessation, glucose control; minimize unnecessary steroid exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Open-angle glaucoma: peripheral field loss, optic disc cupping
Macular degeneration: central distortion, drusen or retinal neovascularization
Acute angle closure: painful red eye, nausea, fixed mid-dilated pupil

table.title: Lens opacity patterns
rows: Central yellowing; myopic shift, temporary reading improvement
Steroids; near vision and bright-light difficulty

cataracts.evidence: Not checked online; established ophthalmology teaching.

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.scope: Central line infection, organisms, line removal, prevention
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.core: Fever or rigors in a patient with an intravascular catheter, especially during infusion, raises concern for catheter-related bacteremia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long catheter dwell time, femoral placement, parenteral nutrition, immunosuppression, hemodialysis
Poor asepsis, frequent hub manipulation; tunneled devices and ports also susceptible

rows.label: Clues
items: Exit-site erythema or drainage may occur; normal insertion-site appearance does not exclude infection
★ **Hypotension, persistent bacteremia**, new murmur, or embolic signs → complicated infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Skin flora migrate externally or contaminated hubs seed intraluminal biofilm
Biofilm limits antibiotic penetration; S aureus and Candida frequently seed distant sites

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Before antibiotics: **paired peripheral and catheter blood cultures**, labelled by source
Same organism with catheter culture positive ≥2 h earlier supports catheter source
Culture removed catheter tip when infection suspected; no routine tip culture after elective removal
Repeat blood cultures to document clearance; persistent positivity → endocarditis, infected thrombus, abscess evaluation
S aureus bacteremia → echocardiography, TEE when high risk; assess metastatic foci

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis → **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, adjusted to cultures and local resistance
★ **Remove line** for shock, tunnel infection, endocarditis, persistent bacteremia, S aureus, Pseudomonas, or fungi
Candida → echinocandin; MSSA → cefazolin or nafcillin; enterococcal treatment follows susceptibilities
Selected stable long-term line infections with coagulase-negative staphylococci → systemic antibiotics + antibiotic lock
Uncomplicated S aureus bacteremia: ≥14 days after clearance; endocarditis/deep infection usually requires 4–6 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Endocarditis, septic thrombophlebitis, osteomyelitis, septic emboli, shock
Unnecessary device retention → relapse; repeated placement → thrombosis and vascular injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hand hygiene, chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximal sterile barrier** during insertion
Scrub hubs, sterile dressings, daily necessity review, prompt removal of unnecessary lines
Avoid routine prophylactic systemic antibiotics or scheduled catheter replacement solely to prevent infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contaminated blood culture: single skin-flora isolate without corroborating cultures or illness
Infusate reaction: temporal symptoms without reproducible bacteremia
Catheter thrombosis: swelling, poor flow; cultures negative unless infected

table.title: Organism pattern
rows: Parenteral nutrition, broad antibiotics; remove catheter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate/calcium deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, pancreatic risk history

cervicitis-pid.name: Cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease
cervicitis-pid.core: Sexually active patient with mucopurulent discharge or postcoital bleeding; ascending infection adds pelvic pain, sometimes an adnexal abscess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condoms, prior STI
IUD-associated PID risk concentrated within first 3 weeks after insertion

rows.label: Clues
items: Cervical friability, easily induced endocervical bleeding; infection sometimes asymptomatic
Dyspareunia, fever; severe unilateral pain/adnexal mass → **tubo-ovarian abscess**
Peritonitis, shock → rupture; RUQ pain → Fitz-Hugh–Curtis perihepatitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GC/CT ascend cervix → endometrium/tubes; PID often polymicrobial, including anaerobes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** first; vaginal/cervical or urine **GC/CT NAAT**; HIV/syphilis testing
★ Pelvic pain + **cervical motion, uterine, OR adnexal tenderness** → presumptive PID; no confirmation delay
Negative cervical NAAT does not exclude upper-tract infection; normal discharge/no vaginal leukocytes argues against PID
**Transvaginal US** for abscess or diagnostic uncertainty; routine laparoscopy unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Cervicitis: empiric GC/CT coverage IF high risk/unreliable follow-up; otherwise await NAAT
★ Admit IF **pregnant, abscess, severe illness**, oral intolerance, uncertain surgical diagnosis, or failure by 72 h
Abscess rupture → emergency surgery; persistent abscess after 48–72 h antibiotics → drainage
Pregnant chlamydia → **azithromycin**, avoid doxycycline; retain IUD initially, reassess if no improvement

rows.label: Complications
items: Tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; abscess → sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from prior **60 days**; abstain until courses completed, partners treated, symptoms resolved
Retest GC/CT at 3 months; pregnant chlamydia → test of cure at 4 weeks
Annual GC/CT screening: sexually active women <25, older women with risks; condoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt unilateral pain, vomiting; Doppler flow may persist
Appendicitis: migrating RLQ pain, CT appendiceal inflammation

table.title: Antibiotic branches
rows: Ceftriaxone; add CT regimen unless excluded
Oral drugs 14 days; ceftriaxone once IM outpatient

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; many microdeletions and sex-chromosome abnormalities arise de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down**: hypotonia, upslanting fissures, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down → **karyotype confirms trisomy 21**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia, leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus with normal chromosomes; either sex
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

clostridioides-difficile-infection.name: Clostridioides difficile infection
clostridioides-difficile-infection.scope: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea, toxic megacolon, pseudomembranous colitis, NAAT vs EIA stool toxin testing, oral fidaxomicin, oral vancomycin, fulminant colitis
clostridioides-difficile-infection.core: Recent antibiotics or healthcare exposure followed by watery diarrhea suggests toxin-mediated colitis; ileus can conceal fulminant disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins; older age, hospitalization, immunosuppression
Prior infection and unnecessary acid suppression increase susceptibility or recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Abdominal cramps, fever, leukocytosis; severe disease may cause AKI and hypoalbuminemia
★ **Hypotension, ileus, or megacolon** defines fulminant infection; diarrhea may disappear

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Antibiotic disruption of microbiota permits spore-forming bacilli to proliferate
Toxins damage colonic epithelium → inflammation and pseudomembranes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Test **unformed stool** with ≥3 unexplained stools/24 hours; exclude laxative effect
NAAT detects toxigenic genes, not active toxin; positive results can represent colonization
Toxin EIA is less sensitive; multistep GDH/NAAT plus toxin improves clinical specificity
No test of cure; abdominal imaging for distention, toxicity, or suspected perforation

rows.label: Tx
items: Stop inciting antibiotic when possible; replace fluids/electrolytes, avoid antimotility drugs in severe colitis
★ Initial nonfulminant infection: **oral fidaxomicin** preferred; oral vancomycin acceptable, usually 10 days
★ Fulminant: **high-dose oral/NG vancomycin + IV metronidazole**; add rectal vancomycin with ileus
Shock, perforation, worsening organ failure → urgent surgical consultation
Recurrence: fidaxomicin or tapered/pulsed vancomycin; multiple recurrences → screened microbiota-based treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Toxic megacolon, perforation, sepsis, recurrent infection
Severe classification: WBC >15,000/µL or creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL; different from fulminant criteria

rows.label: Prevention
items: Contact precautions, gloves/gown, soap-and-water handwashing, sporicidal surface cleaning
Antibiotic stewardship; no screening/treatment of asymptomatic carriers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Laxative-associated diarrhea: medication timing, no inflammatory syndrome
IBD flare: chronic relapsing course; test for coinfection before escalating immunosuppression

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; implants/IUDs provide years of protection; replacement interval depends on product
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel pills sooner preferred

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only method or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, thrombophilia/high-risk VTE**, severe hypertension, early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity; copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

cushing-syndrome.name: Cushing syndrome
cushing-syndrome.scope: Exogenous glucocorticoids, Cushing disease (pituitary adenoma), ectopic ACTH, adrenal adenoma, screening tests (24-hr urine free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, low-dose dexamethasone), high-dose dexamethasone
cushing-syndrome.core: Cortisol excess causes central weight gain with catabolic skin and muscle findings; exclude prescribed steroids before investigating endogenous disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Chronic oral, injected, inhaled, or topical glucocorticoids; interactions can amplify systemic exposure
Pituitary corticotroph adenoma, adrenal tumor; ectopic secretion from small-cell lung cancer or neuroendocrine tumors

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Wide violaceous striae, easy bruising, proximal weakness**, facial plethora
Hypertension, glucose intolerance, menstrual irregularity, hirsutism; children: weight gain with growth failure
Rapid onset, severe hypokalemic alkalosis → marked cortisol excess, often ectopic source

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess glucocorticoid promotes gluconeogenesis, protein breakdown, bone loss, and immune suppression
Very high cortisol overwhelms renal 11β-HSD2 → mineralocorticoid receptor activation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screen: **late-night salivary cortisol ×2**, 24-hour urine free cortisol ×2, or overnight dexamethasone
1 mg overnight dexamethasone: AM cortisol >1.8 µg/dL fails suppression; confirm with another recommended test
Pseudo-Cushing: depression, alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes; random cortisol/ACTH unsuitable screens
★ Confirm excess → **ACTH**; low → adrenal CT, nonsuppressed → pituitary MRI
High-dose dex: pituitary often suppresses, ectopic usually not; uncertain source → inferior petrosal sinus sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exogenous disease → **gradual steroid taper**; abrupt cessation risks adrenal crisis
Pituitary tumor: transsphenoidal surgery; adrenal source: adrenalectomy; ectopic source: tumor-directed treatment
Persistent/unresectable excess → metyrapone or ketoconazole; monitor for adrenal insufficiency and drug toxicity

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis/fracture, infection, VTE, cardiovascular disease, psychiatric illness
Postoperative hypocortisolism → temporary glucocorticoid replacement until axis recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Lowest effective glucocorticoid exposure; bone protection and cardiometabolic risk management
Treat hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, infections; counsel about perioperative thrombosis risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Simple obesity: no progressive skin fragility or objective proximal weakness
PCOS: androgen excess without catabolic stigmata
Pseudo-Cushing: biochemical abnormalities resolve with underlying condition treatment

cushing-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established Endocrine Society diagnostic teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age, family history; vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval with preserved independence; MCI: objective deficit without loss of independent function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in strongly; LR− <0.1 rules out strongly

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.scope: Acute vs chronic DIC, sepsis, malignancy, obstetric complications, coagulopathy (prolonged PT/PTT, low fibrinogen, elevated D-dimer, schistocytes), blood product replacement
disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.core: Systemic coagulation activation simultaneously causes microvascular thrombosis and consumption of platelets/clotting factors, producing organ injury and bleeding.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sepsis, severe trauma/burns, shock, acute pancreatitis
Obstetric emergencies: abruption, amniotic fluid embolism, retained fetal demise
Malignancy: especially acute promyelocytic leukemia, advanced adenocarcinoma; large vascular abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Oozing from IV sites**, mucosal bleeding, widespread ecchymoses in a severely ill patient
Digital ischemia, purpura fulminans, altered mental status, oliguria suggest microthrombi
Chronic compensated disease may present predominantly with venous/arterial thrombosis rather than hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue-factor-driven thrombin generation → fibrin deposition; secondary fibrinolysis increases degradation products
Rapid consumption overwhelms hepatic/marrow replacement in acute disease; slower activation allows partial compensation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **↓Platelets, ↑PT/PTT, ↑D-dimer, ↓fibrinogen**; schistocytes may accompany microangiopathic hemolysis
Serial values and clinical trigger matter; early sepsis can preserve fibrinogen as an acute-phase reactant
CBC/smear, coagulation panel, fibrinogen, renal/liver function; cultures or obstetric evaluation identify cause
ISTH score uses platelets, PT, fibrin marker, fibrinogen; repeat when evolving

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat underlying cause** immediately: antibiotics/source control, obstetric delivery, leukemia-directed treatment
Bleeding or invasive procedure with platelets <50,000/µL → platelet transfusion
★ Bleeding with factor depletion → **FFP**; fibrinogen <100–150 mg/dL → cryoprecipitate
Thrombosis-predominant chronic disease → selected heparin use; avoid during uncontrolled hemorrhage
No blood products solely to normalize labs in nonbleeding stable disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Multiorgan failure, diffuse hemorrhage, limb ischemia/gangrene, death
Transfusion complications: volume overload, lung injury; anticoagulation can worsen bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Prompt sepsis treatment, hemorrhage control, obstetric complication management; monitor high-risk triggers closely

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP/HUS: thrombocytopenia and hemolysis with usually normal PT/PTT
Liver failure: impaired synthesis with hepatic disease; clinical context and trends distinguish
HIT: heparin-linked platelet fall, thrombosis, usually preserved coagulation tests

disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology teaching.

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after starting/changing drugs**, then every 6–12 months; assess adherence
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

elbow-injuries.name: Elbow injuries
elbow-injuries.scope: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus, radial head subluxation, elbow dislocation, fat pad signs, lateral and medial epicondylitis, counterforce bracing, cubital tunnel syndrome
elbow-injuries.core: Age, mechanism, deformity, and precise tenderness separate elbow fracture/dislocation from traction injury, tendinopathy, and nerve compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fall onto outstretched hand → fracture/dislocation; longitudinal forearm pull → pediatric radial-head subluxation
Repetitive wrist loading → epicondylitis; prolonged elbow flexion/pressure → ulnar nerve compression

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, swelling, limited motion after trauma; open wound or tense swelling increases urgency
★ **Absent pulse, cool hand, worsening pain with passive stretch** → vascular injury/compartment syndrome
Check median/anterior interosseous, radial, ulnar function before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pediatric annular-ligament displacement restricts rotation; displaced distal humerus can injure brachial artery
Overuse tendon degeneration differs from inflammatory arthritis; cubital tunnel compresses the ulnar nerve

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Trauma/deformity → **AP/lateral radiographs**; posterior fat pad indicates occult intra-articular fracture
Anterior humeral line missing capitellum supports displaced supracondylar fracture
Classic nursemaid presentation without swelling/bony tenderness → clinical diagnosis; image atypical or failed reduction
Nerve-conduction testing for uncertain or persistent cubital neuropathy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Supracondylar fracture: **splint and urgent orthopedics**; displaced/vascularly compromised → reduction and pinning
Elbow dislocation → reduction, repeat neurovascular examination/films, early supervised motion
★ Nursemaid elbow → **hyperpronation** or supination-flexion; reassess spontaneous arm use
Tendinopathy: rest, NSAIDs, rehabilitation, counterforce brace; cubital tunnel: avoid flexion/pressure, night splint

rows.label: Complications
items: Volkmann ischemic contracture, malunion/cubitus varus, persistent neuropathy
Dislocation → stiffness, instability, heterotopic ossification; immobilization worsens loss of motion

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lift children **under the arms**, avoiding traction on hands/wrists
Ergonomic tools, gradual load progression, stretching/strengthening; pad elbow during repetitive contact

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic joint: fever, effusion, severe passive-motion pain
Radial-head fracture: adult fall, lateral tenderness, painful pronation/supination

table.title: Overuse localization
rows: Medial pain during wrist flexion/pronation against resistance

elbow-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic and peripheral nerve principles.

encephalitis.name: Encephalitis
encephalitis.scope: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1), temporal lobe lesions, CSF analysis (elevated RBCs, lymphocytic pleocytosis, PCR), IV acyclovir, West Nile virus, autoimmune encephalitis
encephalitis.core: Fever with sustained altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits suggests brain inflammation and warrants immediate empiric acyclovir.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HSV-1 often occurs without immunosuppression; mosquito exposure suggests arboviruses
Autoimmune disease or tumor association; anti-NMDA receptor disease sometimes accompanies ovarian teratoma

rows.label: Clues
items: HSV: personality change, aphasia, olfactory hallucinations, focal seizures
★ **Temporal lobe abnormalities** strongly suggest HSV; hemorrhagic CSF possible but not required
West Nile: movement disorder or asymmetric flaccid weakness; anti-NMDA: psychosis, dyskinesia, autonomic instability
Reduced consciousness, status epilepticus, or respiratory compromise → ICU-level care

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV causes necrotizing inflammation, often limbic/temporal; mosquito-borne viruses infect neuronal tissue
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface antigens disrupt synaptic signaling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **LP: CSF cells, protein, glucose, HSV PCR**; lymphocytes, ↑protein, usually normal glucose
Neuroimaging before LP for focal deficits, papilledema, marked impaired consciousness, or suspected mass effect
MRI more sensitive than CT; EEG identifies nonconvulsive seizures or temporal periodic discharges
Early negative PCR with strong suspicion → continue treatment and repeat CSF PCR in 3–7 days
West Nile: CSF IgM; autoimmune suspicion → CSF/serum antibodies and tumor search

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected HSV → **IV acyclovir immediately**, usually 14–21 days; do not await PCR
Airway/seizure support; possible bacterial infection → ceftriaxone + vancomycin; Listeria risk → add ampicillin
Acyclovir: renal adjustment, IV hydration; West Nile: supportive care
★ Autoimmune disease → **steroids, IVIG/plasma exchange**, tumor removal after infectious evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent memory impairment, epilepsy, focal deficits, death; acyclovir crystal nephropathy
Severe autoimmune disease: arrhythmia, hypoventilation, prolonged rehabilitation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mosquito repellent, protective clothing, vector control; no routine HSV encephalitis vaccine

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic CSF, low glucose; overlap requires empiric coverage
Toxic/metabolic delirium: systemic explanation without inflammatory CSF
Primary psychosis: lacks new seizures, dysautonomia, or focal neurologic abnormalities

encephalitis.evidence: Not checked online; established infectious and autoimmune neurology teaching.

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation; cholecystectomy → bile-duct injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.scope: Nephritic syndrome, poststreptococcal GN, IgA nephropathy, rapidly progressive GN (anti-GBM, ANCA), lupus nephritis, RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria quantification, kidney biopsy
glomerulonephritis.core: Glomerular inflammation causes hematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, edema, and reduced filtration; rapidly rising creatinine demands urgent evaluation for crescentic disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent streptococcal pharyngitis/skin infection, systemic autoimmunity, small-vessel vasculitis
IgA nephropathy often follows mucosal infection; anti-GBM pulmonary bleeding risk increases with smoking

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs** identify a glomerular bleeding source
Tea-colored urine, oliguria, periorbital swelling; nephrotic-range protein loss can coexist
★ **Hemoptysis + AKI** → pulmonary–renal syndrome; rapidly progressive disease may initially lack systemic symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune complexes, basement-membrane antibodies, or pauci-immune vascular injury inflame glomerular capillaries
Crescent formation compresses capillary tufts → rapid, potentially irreversible loss of filtration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Urinalysis/microscopy → **creatinine, electrolytes, urine protein/creatinine ratio**; monitor urine output
C3/C4, ANA/dsDNA, ANCA, anti-GBM; ASO/anti-DNase B when poststreptococcal disease suspected
★ **Kidney biopsy** for rapidly progressive AKI, substantial persistent proteinuria, or uncertain systemic GN
Typical childhood poststreptococcal course may not require biopsy; persistent low C3 beyond 8 weeks warrants reassessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Salt restriction, loop diuretics for overload, BP control; ACE inhibitor/ARB for persistent proteinuria when stable
★ Pulmonary–renal/RPGN → **urgent nephrology, steroids + immunosuppression** before irreversible decline
Anti-GBM: plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide; ANCA: rituximab/cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange only selected severe cases
Lupus: biopsy-directed mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide + steroids; poststreptococcal disease mainly supportive

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, hypertensive emergency, CKD; dialysis for refractory life-threatening derangements
Immunosuppression → infection, cytopenias, infertility with cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP/proteinuria, avoid nephrotoxins, follow renal function and urine findings

rows.label: Mimics
